A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OLMoE grokking study. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations, and appendices are readable, and relocated theoretical and experimental material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original OLMoE checkpoint analyses, downstream-performance correlations in Table 1, and a synthetic MoE experiment in Appendix A.4.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds aggregate pathway trajectories and parameter-dynamics results in Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed Levenshtein pathway-distance and cross-layer cosine-consistency metrics retain their constructions. v3 clarifies token averaging and expert ranking without establishing a change to the monitoring algorithm or model.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same math, code, commonsense, and chemistry coverage, including DART-Math, HumanEval+, CommonsenseQA, and MMLU college chemistry. Pretraining, validation, instruction-tuning sources, and the synthetic Gaussian-cluster experiment are retained; the consolidated dataset table does not introduce new coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 and Figure 7 retain the same comparison methods: training loss, moving-average training loss, and validation loss. Appendix D compares internal parameter types, rather than adding a competing monitoring method.

E3.justification: As written, v3 Section 3.1 requires loss stability relative to the final checkpoint at every subsequent checkpoint; v1 required persistently low loss but stated the stability condition only at the candidate onset. Appendix D also introduces a parameter-norm snapshot protocol for measuring convergence and stability. These reported changes do not establish that existing experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v3 adds aggregate pathway trends in Figures 4 and 6 and a focused analysis of whether routing evolution accompanies router, expert, or attention updates in Appendix D. The existing layerwise analysis and synthetic edit-distance/effective-dimension analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions retain Pearson/Spearman significance reporting and independently initialized synthetic routers with a plotted plus/minus one-standard-deviation band. No new replication counts or uncertainty procedures are reported. Appendix D's stability statistic measures temporal dynamics rather than uncertainty across experimental replications.

E6.justification: v3 adds aggregate trajectories and Table 3: router/expert/attention convergence speeds are 0.151/0.063/0.083, with stabilities 5.63/7.32/6.01. Table 1's correlations and Figure 7's regression results are unchanged. The synthetic scatterplot is redisplayed on a normalized scale without establishing a new experimental outcome.

T1.justification: The formal memorization criterion strengthens the stability requirement from the candidate onset to all subsequent checkpoints. Otherwise, Theorem 4.1 and the fixed-routing NTK assumptions, bound, and proof are mathematically retained as Appendix A moves to Appendix C; the added next-token-loss formula explains an existing objective.

C1.justification: The claims of asynchronous local grokking and training-data-only generalization monitoring remain. v3 strengthens the practical efficiency claim from efficient computation to zero or almost-zero monitoring cost in the abstract and introduction, without adding a cost measurement.

C2.justification: v3 explains that one-pass 'memorization' can include interpolation before a sample is encountered and distinguishes token-level fit from downstream task generalization. Appendix D adds a fast-router/slow-expert interpretation. The conclusion removes v1's explicit single-architecture and one-layer-NTK limitations and proposes virtual pathways in dense models as future work.

D1.justification: v3 specifies token-averaged routing weights and expert ranking, explicitly states the ten-checkpoint sampling design, and documents three instruction-tuning epochs for commonsense/domain-specific evaluation. Appendix D explains its norm-based metric computation. These are mainly disclosures; the existing hardware, LoRA hyperparameters, dataset sources, and contamination-filtering instructions are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Wang et al.'s Grokked Transformers Are Implicit Reasoners to the mechanism discussion, and cites He et al.'s residual networks and Li and Zhou's Sparser Mixture-of-Adapters to motivate cross-layer comparability. The broader positioning against small-model, synthetic-task grokking studies remains.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and substantial portions of Sections 3–4 are rewritten. Section 3 is reorganized around LLM-specific challenges and an explicit measurement framework, terminology shifts from 'grokking data' to memorized samples, and the appendices are reordered. This substantially changes the narrative despite retaining most scientific content.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 gain global panels; the schematic, axes, legends, and captions are refined. Figure A.1 becomes normalized Figure 8, dataset Tables A.1–A.2 merge into Table 2, and Table 3 is added. The main plotting designs and document layout remain recognizable.

improvement.justification: v3 clarifies the central distinction between token-level memorization and downstream generalization, improves routing-metric documentation, and adds a focused parameter-dynamics diagnostic. These provide limited gains in interpretability and reproducibility while the core correlations and NTK proof remain unchanged. Removing explicit limitations and strengthening unmeasured zero-cost claims partly offsets those gains.
